issues.legal_issue: An executing court may order the removal of construction unlawfully raised during a suit to give effect to a final decree for possession, even when the decree contains no express mandatory injunction for demolition.
material_facts: A final decree declared the decree-holder the owner of the property and directed the judgment-debtor and those occupying through him to deliver vacant possession.
While the suit was pending, the judgment-debtor constructed shops on the property without the court’s permission and inducted tenants.
The bailiff could not execute the possession warrant because of the shops and the occupants, and the decree-holder sought their removal in the execution proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The executing court had power to direct demolition of the shops and delivery of vacant possession; a separate suit for a mandatory injunction was unnecessary.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 21 Rule 35(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure, an executing court may make incidental, ancillary, or necessary orders to enforce a decree for possession, including removing a superstructure raised pendente lite. Order 21 Rule 101 requires relevant questions arising in the execution proceeding to be determined there rather than through a separate suit; the court also referred to its inherent power under Section 151. The owner’s right to possession and enjoyment includes a remedy to remove an obstruction that would frustrate execution. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: possession_decree_in_execution and decree_is_final and construction_was_raised_during_suit_without_court_permission and construction_obstructs_delivery

predicates.possession_decree_in_execution: A court is enforcing a decree that requires delivery of possession of property.
predicates.decree_is_final: The decree for possession has become final.
predicates.construction_was_raised_during_suit_with: The judgment-debtor or someone claiming through that person raised construction on the property while the suit was pending and without the court’s permission.
predicates.construction_obstructs_delivery: The construction prevents or obstructs delivery of possession under the decree.

issues.definition: When a final possession decree is being enforced and unauthorized construction raised during the suit obstructs delivery, the rule permits the executing court to order its removal.

issues.legal_issue: Occupants inducted by a judgment-debtor during the suit and claiming through that judgment-debtor are bound by the possession decree and need not have been individually joined in the suit.
material_facts: The judgment-debtor constructed shops on the disputed property while the suit was pending and inducted tenants into possession without the court’s permission.
The tenants claimed possession through the judgment-debtor and their occupation obstructed delivery under the final decree for possession.
issues.conclusion: The tenants were bound by the decree despite not being individually joined as defendants, and their presence did not prevent removal of the obstruction and delivery of possession.
issues.legal_principle: A person claiming title, right, or interest through a judgment-debtor, including under the colour of an interest derived from that person, is bound by the decree and need not be impleaded individually. Under Order 21 Rule 35(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure, after reasonable warning, the executing officers may take necessary steps to put the decree-holder in possession, including removing an obstruction. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.possession_decree_in_execution: A court is enforcing a decree that requires delivery of possession of property.
predicates.occupants_entered_through_judgment_debto: The occupants took possession during the suit through the judgment-debtor or claim an interest through that person.
predicates.occupants_obstruct_delivery: The occupants’ possession prevents or obstructs delivery under the decree.

issues.definition: When occupants who entered through the judgment-debtor during the suit obstruct enforcement of a possession decree, they are bound by the decree without having been individually joined.
